pharm: Cytidine nucleoside analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitor (HIV-1 and HBV activity)
quick: HIV-1: 300 mg once daily or 150 mg twice daily (with other antiretrovirals). HBV (Epivir-HBV): 100 mg once daily
May take with or without food
Used in pregnancy as part of antiretroviral therapy; enroll in Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry
Breastfeeding not recommended in HIV (US); lamivudine is excreted in milk
Dose reduction required for CrCl <50 mL/min
No adjustment for lamivudine alone; caution - HBV flare on discontinuation
No direct interaction; limit due to underlying liver disease
HIV viral load/CD4; LFTs; in HBV-coinfected, monitor for hepatitis flare after stopping
summary: Lamivudine (3TC) is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used in combination with other antiretrovirals to treat HIV-1, and (as a lower-dose product) to treat chronic hepatitis B. It is generally well tolerated. Key cautions: dose reduction in renal impairment, risk of HBV exacerbation on discontinuation in coinfected patients, and the class warning of lactic acidosis/hepatomegaly with steatosis.
indications: Treatment of HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents
Treatment of chronic hepatitis B (lower-dose Epivir-HBV product)

dosage.d: 300 mg once daily OR 150 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Always use in combination ART; dosage here is for HIV, not HBV

dosage.d: Weight-based, up to 5 mg/kg twice daily or 10 mg/kg once daily (per label tables)
dosage.t: Twice or once daily per regimen
dosage.n: Max 300 mg/day; use scored tablet/solution per weight bands
HBV dose is lower; do not use HBV product alone in HIV/HBV coinfection

admin: Use the correct product/dose for the indication (HIV vs HBV products differ)
Confirm HIV status before using HBV product (and vice versa) in possibly coinfected patients
Reduce dose per CrCl in renal impairment
moa: Lamivudine is intracellularly phosphorylated to its active 5'-triphosphate metabolite, which is incorporated into viral DNA by reverse transcriptase, causing chain termination. It thereby inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase and HBV polymerase.

relative: HIV/HBV coinfection if not on adequate combined regimen (resistance/flare risk)
monitor: Lactic acidosis signs in at-risk patients

preg: Lamivudine is used during pregnancy as a component of antiretroviral therapy. A pregnancy exposure registry (Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry, 1-800-258-4263) monitors outcomes.
lact: Lamivudine is excreted in human milk. In the US, breastfeeding is not recommended for women with HIV because of the risk of HIV transmission and potential adverse reactions.
renal: Dosage reduction is required for CrCl <50 mL/min (reduced dose/interval per label); accumulates in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment needed for lamivudine itself. In patients with HBV (or HIV/HBV coinfection), severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B can occur on discontinuation - monitor liver function for several months after stopping.

major: Concomitant emtricitabine (similar analogue - do not combine; no added benefit, overlapping resistance)
moderate: Sorbitol-containing co-medications reduce lamivudine exposure (avoid chronic co-administration)
Cladribine (lamivudine may interfere with intracellular activation)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No direct pharmacologic interaction; limit alcohol given underlying liver disease
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor HIV RNA/CD4, HBV markers, LFTs, renal function, CBC

serious: Lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (class effect, can be fatal)
Pancreatitis (especially in pediatric patients with risk factors)
Severe acute HBV exacerbation on discontinuation in HBV/coinfected patients
emergency: Lactic acidosis (rapid breathing, abdominal pain, profound fatigue)
Severe hepatic decompensation from HBV flare

monitoring: HIV-1 RNA viral load and CD4 count
Liver function tests (and HBV markers in coinfected patients, including after stopping)
CBC; serum amylase/lipase if pancreatitis suspected
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed; do not run out (resistance/flare risk if doses missed)
Do not stop without medical advice - hepatitis B can flare badly
Report severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness, fast breathing, or yellowing of skin/eyes
This medicine controls but does not cure HIV; continue safer-sex/transmission precautions
Tell all providers you take this so doses are not duplicated with similar drugs
pk: Antiviral effect over days to weeks (viral load decline)
Plasma ~5-7 h; intracellular triphosphate longer (supports once-daily HIV dosing)
Tablets 25 C; oral solution store at 20-25 C
pearls: The fixed-dose lamivudine/zidovudine combination carries a boxed warning (hematologic toxicity, myopathy, lactic acidosis/hepatomegaly, HBV exacerbations) - the hematologic/myopathy components derive from zidovudine, not lamivudine alone.
Do NOT use the lower-dose HBV product (100 mg) as sole HIV therapy and do not combine lamivudine with emtricitabine (overlapping analogues).
In HIV/HBV coinfection, stopping lamivudine can trigger a severe hepatitis B flare - monitor LFTs for months after discontinuation.
M184V resistance mutation reduces lamivudine activity but increases susceptibility to zidovudine/tenofovir and decreases viral fitness.
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. Consistent adherence is critical to prevent resistance.
overdose: There is no known specific antidote. Limited experience; treat supportively with monitoring and standard measures. Lamivudine is removed to a limited extent by hemodialysis/peritoneal dialysis (continuous hemodialysis has been used in overdose support).
